answer.label: Not Alexander Hamilton — a modern proverb
answer.sourceLine: There is no substantive evidence here for the American statesman. Quote Investigator treats the saying as an anonymous modern proverb, with a close match printed under Gordon A. Eadie’s name in January 1945. Source and attribution evidence ↗

source.excerpt: Those who stand for nothing, fall for anything
trail: There is no substantive evidence here for the American statesman. Quote Investigator treats the saying as an anonymous modern proverb, with a close match printed under Gordon A. Eadie’s name in January 1945. Source and attribution evidence ↗

Its exact short form was credited to the British broadcaster Alex Hamilton in 1978. That later Hamilton is a different person; Eadie’s use also does not prove that he coined the proverb. Read the supporting source ↗
